name: Dogoso
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalogue, 'OLAC resources in and about the Dogoso language' (Internet Archive copy 2019-12-12).
sources.note: Lists only the Glottolog and Ethnologue records: no archive holdings, no SIL literacy materials, no recordings for Dogoso.

sources.citation: Tauxier, Louis. 1931. Vocabulaires Dorhosié et Dorhosié-Finng [with 'Comparaison du Dorhosié avec le Guin, le Sénoufo, etc.', pp. 107-110]. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 1(1): 87-110.
sources.note: The first and only open primary data on Dogoso: a 639-item Dorhosié-Finng wordlist taken in January 1922 ('Premier vocabulaire Dorhosié-Finng qui ait été pris'), in French practical spelling with no accent or tone marks and no remark of any kind on prosody; pp. 107-110 are comparison tables (image-only on Persée).
sources.venue: Journal de la Société des Africanistes

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2014. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 17th ed., entry 'Dogoso' [dgs]. Dallas: SIL International (Internet Archive copy 2014).
sources.note: Nothing; alternate names, six villages in Comoé province, 9,000 speakers (1999 SIL), lexical similarity 56% Khe / 15% Dogosé / 16% Khisa, 'Dialects: none known'; no typology line.

sources.citation: Labouret, Henri. 1958. Nouvelles notes sur les tribus du rameau lobi: leurs migrations, leur évolution, leurs parlers et ceux de leurs voisins. Mémoires de l'IFAN 54. Dakar: IFAN. 295 pp.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.locator: Part IV, Vocabulaires comparés doro et gan, Remarque préliminaire, printed p. 279; numeration table 'Dorosié / Dorosié-Fing / Gan' printed p. 281; vocabularies…
sources.note: Contains a 'Dorosie-Fing' (= Dogoso) wordlist with Labouret's phonetic conventions; his IFAN notes sometimes carry a remark on accent/tone in the transcription preface. Scan only in Hammarström's collection (bestfn); not on archive.org, Gallica or HathiTrust.

sources.citation: Labouret, Henri. 1931. Les tribus du rameau lobi. Travaux et mémoires de l'Institut d'Ethnologie 15. Paris: Institut d'Ethnologie. vii+510 pp.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.note: Early ethnography with Dorossié(-Fing) vocabulary; low chance of a prosodic statement; Gallica SRU and archive.org return nothing, HathiTrust blocked.
sources.venue: Travaux et mémoires de l'Institut d'Ethnologie

sources.citation: Tauxier, Louis. 1931. Les Dorhosié et Dorhosié-Finng du cercle de Bobo-Dioulasso (Soudan français). Journal de la Société des Africanistes 1(1): 61-86.
sources.note: Ethnography of the Dorhosié (= Dogosé) and Dorhosié-Finng (= Dogoso, pp. 77-86); nothing on pronunciation, tone or accent (a full-text search for stress/accent/ton/syllab/prononc: only a scarification simile 'accent aigu' p. 63). scanned text harvested from Persée page endpoints by the dogo1295 check, copied here.
sources.venue: Journal de la Société des Africanistes

sources.citation: Wikipedia articles 'Dogoso language' (en), 'Dogoso' (de, fr); Wikidata Q35343.
sources.note: Stubs; no phonology and no bibliography beyond Ethnologue/SIL.

In Gudrun Miehe & Kerstin Winkelmann (eds.), Noun class systems in Gur languages, Vol. I: Southwestern Gur languages (without Gurunsi) (Gur Monographs 9), ca. pp. 194-208; with C3. sources.note: The only first-hand modern description of Dogoso by its sole fieldworker (SFB 268 Frankfurt); the parallel chapters open with phonological remarks on tone and (for Kaasa, Khisa) stress. Google's full-volume index shows no 'stress'/'accent' hit in this chapter, so it will most likely give only a tone statement -- but that is the best there is. Google Books snippet view (id 2IQLAQAAMAAJ) and HathiTrust mdp.39015079239599 (search-only) were both bot-could not be reached by automated download; publisher PDF sold by Köppe / Clavis Aurea.
sources.venue: Noun class systems in Gur languages, Vol

sources.note: Bibliography only: Glottolog has no grammar, sketch, phonology or dictionary of Dogoso; its Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are Miehe & Winkelmann 2007 (rated phonology or text collection), Labouret 1958 and Tauxier 1931 (a wordlist or less). Labouret 1931/1958 and Armstrong n.d. exist only as scans in Hammarström's private collection.
